summary: Count small groups of up to 5 and know how many there are.
See how many are in a group of up to 4 at a glance, without counting.
Understand and use words for zero, like none or nothing, when there are no things left.
Link numbers to the amounts they stand for, using real objects and simple drawings.
Tell numbers apart from letters and recognize some of the written numbers 0 to 9.
Say the counting numbers out loud in order from 1 to 10.
Say the number that comes next, up to 9, when someone starts counting for you.
Understand that putting groups together or splitting them apart gives a new number.
Count out a set number of objects, up to 5, when asked for that many.
Say the new number when small groups, up to 5, are put together or some are taken away.
Work out simple number problems that come up in play and daily routines.
Share up to 10 things fairly between two children so each gets the same.
Make a sensible guess about how many things are in a small group.
Compare two groups to see if they're equal or which has more, in a way the child chooses.
Describe comparisons with words like more, less, fewer, the same as and equal to.
Compare, order and describe objects by one feature, like which is longer or taller.
Measure how long or how full things are with everyday units, like hands, blocks or scoops.
Use words like tall, short, heavy, light, empty and full to describe and compare things.
Start to sense time by knowing the order of the day, like nap comes after lunch.
Guess how many scoops or blocks something will take in play, then check by counting.
With a teacher's help, try real measuring tools like rulers, scales and measuring tapes.
Know that length, weight and time are each measured in their own kinds of units.
Sort, order, compare and describe objects by features such as color, size or shape.
Spot, copy, continue and make simple patterns with objects, sounds or movements.
With an adult's help, show a repeating pattern by saying it aloud or building it with objects.
Name common flat and solid shapes and describe them, like how many sides or if lines curve.
Sort a mix of flat and solid shapes by kind: triangles, circles, cubes, spheres and so on.
Name the flat faces of solid shapes with flat-shape names, like a cube has square faces.
Put flat shapes together to make new ones, like two triangles into a square.
Picture how a shape will look when it is turned or flipped, like upside down.
Show where things are and which place they hold in a line, like first or last.
Use words for where things are and for order in a line, like under, beside, first and next.
With a teacher's help, think of questions that can be answered by collecting information.
Collect information about themselves and things around them to answer a question.
With help, sort and show information with objects, pictures and simple graphs, and talk about it.
With help, guess what the results will be before collecting information.
Say how likely something is with words like possible, impossible, always and never.
